As the institute celebrated its 60th anniversary, YAN, the young acousticians’ network of the European Acoustics Association (EAA), launched a series of short illustrated profiles touring acoustics laboratories across Europe. The first stop is the Institute for Hearing Technology and Acoustics (IHTA) at RWTH Aachen University, and Fanyu Meng reposted the eight slides for his readers.

IHTA belongs to RWTH’s Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology and, under Janina Fels and Michael Vorländer, works across hearing technology and technical acoustics. Its topics range from audio-visual interaction, auditory scene analysis, binaural technology, hearing technology in biomedical engineering, noise research and psychoacoustics to acoustic measurement, acoustic virtual reality, electroacoustics, vibroacoustics, numerical acoustics, and room and building acoustics. Facilities include anechoic and hemi-anechoic chambers, reverberation rooms, and labs for virtual reality and complex sound reproduction.

Its lectures are part of the bachelor’s and master’s programs in electrical engineering and information technology, from an introduction to acoustics to technical acoustics, hearing technology, audiology and voice, and acoustic virtual reality; students of architecture, physics and mechanical engineering can attend too. Bachelor’s courses are taught in German and master’s courses in English. The institute also shares free tools, including the ITA-Toolbox, the Virtual Acoustics (VA) auralization framework and the ITApp for interactive teaching, and YAN recommends it as a great place to do a PhD.

Reposted by Fanyu Meng from the series “An European Tour Across Acoustics Laboratories” by the EAA Young Acousticians Network (YAN). The institute’s website is www.akustik.rwth-aachen.de.
